articles.title: Volunteers Turn Out for the Fall Cleanup Across Foundry Row
articles.deck: Residents of Foundry Row filled the hall on Sunday to ask questions about the plan.
body: The plan calls for winter coat drive along Fox Terrace, with work expected to start in April. The Foundry Row Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
The group has raised $25,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.
Dana Jurgens, who has lived in Foundry Row for 15 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. Public works estimates the work will take about 15 weeks once it begins.

body: To the editor: I have lived on Reed Court for 24 years, and I want to say what a difference the Hickory Ridge Recreation Center has made.

articles.title: Janet Ingersoll, 95, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Janet Ingersoll for the many years of service to Kettle Hill.
body: Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Kettle Hill.

Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Kettle Hill Block Association in his or her name. Janet Ingersoll died in November at home on Sawmill Drive, at the age of 95.

Born in Kettle Hill in the years after the war, Janet Ingersoll spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood. Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Kettle Hill.

articles.deck: Supporters and opponents on Orion Avenue disagreed about cost and timing.
body: Residents of Marsh Landing said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Public works estimates the work will take about 35 weeks once it starts in January.

Councilmember Ellis Renner asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $18,500. Residents of Marsh Landing said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.
